reviews.text: In the hands of a different, more confident director, Boston Strangler could have been fantastic. As it is, it just feels like Zodiac-lite, with very little to make it memorable despite a compelling mystery at its core.
reviews.author: Tom Spoors

reviews.text: Because real life events don’t unfold in three acts, the film feels repetitive and at times aimless.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: Matt Ruskin’s film dials down on fetishizing murderous men to tell the story of women who might just see them for who they really are.
reviews.author: Manik Sharma

reviews.text: Director Matt Ruskin, who also wrote the screenplay, has created a serviceable film which while concentrating on sexism, feminism and many other “isms”, forgets the basics of telling a thrilling story
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: Thanks to fine performances by Knightley and Coon, Ruskin’s script demonstrates how McLaughlin and Cole prevailed over overt misogynistic attitudes as well as subtle but implicit gender biases and microaggressions.
reviews.author: Lee Zumpe

reviews.text: There is a quietly persistent, simmering and incendiary flare to this film, which, by virtue of Knightley's knowing performance and the well-written script, feels tired and afraid.
reviews.author: Alisha Mughal

reviews.text: At a time when seemingly every streaming service debuts new true-crime programming on a weekly basis, “Boston Strangler” stands far above the crowd.
reviews.author: Kevin Slane

reviews.text: Matt Ruskin’s Investigative thriller limps and shudders like the victims it details, making one wish they were watching the films that inspired it instead.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: Here is the film that She Said so desperately tried to tell us it was - at least on the journalism side of things. Strong lead characters, especially by Keira Knightley, navigating sexism that is as inherent in solving the case as reporting it.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: It lacks empathy, humanity, and insight, and strands Keira Knightley and Carrie Coon in a dry retelling of a famously frustrating serial killer case.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: It’s a diverting enough package, but only if you consider the Googling rabbit hole you’ll fall into afterward as an integral part of the genre’s make-up. As you should.
reviews.author: Michael Atkinson

reviews.text: This has to be one of the worst looking movies I can remember.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: At home, you can kind of appreciate that, hey, this knockoff Zodiac has some good talent on it.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: An oddly inert and even old-fashioned yarn, one that sleepwalks for long stretches, defusing much of the drama of what is an undeniably fascinating true-crime story.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Lacks tension and excitement and ends with a highly speculative conclusion that strains for profundity it fails to reach....But it does offer a credible portrait of the two women...who struggled...to push the investigation forward.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Boston Strangler could have done so much more to make their story feel more vital without undermining their success with conspiracy theories and half-explained alternate suspects. Boston Strangler is a decent story that could have been so much better.
reviews.author: Alex Maidy

reviews.text: a decent journalism time capsule that aligns more with 2015’s Spotlight than with a suspenseful thriller like Silence of the Lambs.
reviews.author: Valerie Kalfrin

reviews.text: The film’s depiction of sexism is blunt, but never preachy or didactic, and the performances by Knightley and Coon ground their characters’ actions in a stark reality of inequality.
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: It’s quite effortlessly unnerving when it desires to be, but there’s a surprising lack of risk taking with a story that should’ve indulged in the unpredictable.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Keira Knightley brings fresh life to this old story.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: In a world where Netflix is pumping out low-effort true-crime doc content on a weekly basis, Boston Strangler is a sterling example of how it should be done.
reviews.author: Clement Tyler Obropta

reviews.text: The work of journalists like Loretta McLaughlin in situations like the one depicted is invaluable, and this film deftly shows exactly why.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: ... Not only it delivers a revealing feminist take but also a theory around the crimes themselves, in addition to respectfully paying tribute to the 1967 film and Fleischer. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: It might not reach [the heights of ZODIAC or SPOTLIGHT] due in part to the continued mystery surrounding the murder spree, but it maintains intrigue thanks to an effectively determined Knightley.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: An excellent pairing of Keira Knightley and Carrie Coon.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: There was enough material to build a compelling thriller, but, and there's always a but when things don't entirely round off, here, the fear isn't palpable... It doesn't exist. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Boston Stranger is smart and, perhaps to a fault, measured and steady.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: A well-shot & acted film about two women journalists trying to hold institutions accountable when they failed to protect the women of their city at their most vulnerable. Which in many ways connects now to what happened then.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Though Boston Strangler isn’t as gripping as other real-life stories based on serial killers, it’s worth the watch if you’re an avid true crime fan.
reviews.author: Ready Steady Cut Staff

reviews.text: Written and directed by Matt Ruskin, this period thriller and biopic portrays ’60s Boston with grim color palettes and scrupulous detail. Every attempt at a Boston accent is spot on, and the excellent cast embodies their characters’ speech and mannerisms.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: For the most part, Ruskin proceeds in a prosaic fashion that tends to drag. What feels like a dutiful approach to storytelling often robs the movie of opportunities to sizzle.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: The movie’s “Zodiac” running on fewer cylinders, with many pointed things to say about the difficulties faced by working women in the early 1960s but a lugubrious narrative structure that sprawls and wanders and eventually sputters out.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: The acting is expressive and engaging, especially from Knightley and Coon, who have a strained dynamic that works to make their relationship even more believable.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: The media is often criticised for using “sensationalised” headlines to grab attention in modern times, but the two journalists used this tool to get officials and police to listen to how dire the situation was.
reviews.author: Emma Clark-Dow

reviews.text: It’s refreshing to see two women crack the case after a century of male detectives. Examples are all too rare and recent, from Jodie Foster and Kasi Lemmons in “The Silence of the Lambs" to Zoe Kazan and Carey Mulligan in the underrated “She Said."
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Boston Strangler serves as a capable filmmaking exercise as well as an acting one.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: Ruskin manages to pay tribute to Loretta Laughlin and Jean Cole's hard work but isn't as successful in completing the story.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Knightley and Coon duet with the lived-in feel of a seasoned screen pairing.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: Coon has done a lot of supporting work, and it’s great to see her stretch out more here. She and Cooper are superb, as is Ruskin’s recreation of 1960s Boston.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: A drab affair confined to shallow focus and a battery of performances all in the same key. Yet, Ruskin’s new take finds resonance and takes time to consider the experience of the victims. “What must that have been like for her?” McLaughlin asks.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: The matchup of Keira Knightly and Carrie Coon punches up this involving, period-rich but somewhat ordinary thriller that celebrates old-school journalism.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Carrie Coon  and Keira Knightly are equally yoked in  strength, vulnerability and tenacity explored through two women fighting it out and standing their ground amongst a male chauvinistic world of journalism. Moves a little slow, but well worth the ride
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: While admiration comes with adapting an important story, the delivery doesn’t seem to be up to the challenge.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Even if getting fine performances by Keira and Carrie, and being correct on the social issues--it's bland and lacks suspense.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: It's not as good as Spotlight or Zodiac, but it's perfectly involving.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: Boston Strangler features intelligent performances and some accurate rendering of mid-century gender inequality. I
reviews.author: Jennifer Green

reviews.text: Keira Knightley leads a strong cast in Boston Strangler, who all lend real watchability to this true crime tale even as its pendulous air and brooding soundtrack begin to get a little suffocating.
reviews.author: Johnny Loftus

reviews.text: Knightley, in a performance as crisp as the corners of an envelope, makes McLaughlin’s perseverance—and the pressures she faced as she also tried to be a good wife and mother—deeply believable.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: The film... mostly works, thanks to Ruskin’s other angle: interrogating how the meaning of this story changes over time.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: …Boston Strangler is a good addition to the true crime genre of films if only because it pushes the audience to question who the narration is coming from.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Boston Strangler is precisely the kind of media Kilgariff described as cold, one whose immense effort goes toward the tired staples of period recreation and carefully laid out plot beats instead of contending with reality.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: Decent and fascinatingly structured true crime story, combining SHE SAID with PSYCHO. and Keira Knightley strikes a nice balance as a conflicted reporter. However, there were several "newspaper movie" cliches, including the nicknaming of a woman as kid.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: The stars’ performances are rather wasted, though, in Matt Ruskin’s film, which blurs the story’s timeline without creating purposeful drama.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: It's Neo-Noir aesthetic gains strength as the investigation progresses. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: Although all the elements are there for a spine-tingling Zodiac-style mystery thriller, the film fails to build any real momentum and ends up completely running out of steam.
reviews.author: Elizabeth Gregory

reviews.text: The reliance on the shot-through-a-dirty-fishtank look ultimately starts undercutting what is good about the movie: the work of its leads.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: Though the Boston Strangler case itself is undoubtedly a gripping one and the cast delivers all-around solid performances, the shaky direction and lackluster script hold this period thriller back from being truly memorable.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: Matt Ruskin's Boston Strangler is an unfocused mess, unsure of the tale it's supposed to be.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: The adrenaline rush of investigative work is divorced from Boston Strangler, leaving viewers to be compelled by the authentic (but not particularly entertaining) paperwork of the job.
reviews.author: Mónica Marie Zorrilla

reviews.text: For fans of the true crime genre, Boston Strangler will provide an adequate retelling of this classic case with strong performances and a unique perspective.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Sturdily satisfies as a movie, even when keeping things simple and straightforward.
reviews.author: Marshall Shaffer

reviews.text: “Boston Strangler” capably captures the considerable frustrations of the investigation as well as the frustrations of sexism and corruption.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: By the end, let's just call it another well-done showcase for the kind of tough, investigative journalism that rarely exists today, even if the entire film is not quite on par with last year's "She Said."
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Matt Ruskin’s “Boston Strangler” can be seen as an update, and something of a rebuke, to the 1968 movie “The Boston Strangler.”
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: …The 2023 Boston Strangler handles potentially exploitative material in a non-lurid way, and generally doesn’t stoop to melodrama, keeping its focus on a sobering truth; that women are seen by many men as an inferior sex, even in death…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: With respectful and valiant intentions, Matt Ruskin’s film "Boston Strangler" seeks to place the important heroes alongside, and ultimately higher than, the more famous villains they chased.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: This true-life crime drama has almost everything you could possibly want from a sharp revisionist thriller.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: While a compelling look at the case and the journalistic process, the deliberately dark presentation and murky approach leaves a lot to be desired.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: There's a satisfying irony in two women chasing a man targeting women, but really their main antagonists are the obstructive (and apparently useless) police department.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: This is one of those movies that finds a fresh way into an age-old story you might think you already knew but clearly didn’t. Bravo.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Boston Strangler may appeal to those interested in the historical case or the true-crime genre, but it never justifies the need to adapt this real story into a fictionalized film.
reviews.author: Breeze Riley

reviews.text: If it's formulaic and familiar, well perhaps that’s because viewers are saturated with stories of men who kill women, and women who have to kick against the system to get their voices heard.
reviews.author: Rosie Fletcher

reviews.text: Writer-director Matt Ruskin nicely captures both the hurdles and indignities Loretta faced as a woman in this male-dominated world and the palpable fear that gripped the city, another echo of Zodiac.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: By effective design, the most startling aspect of #BostonStrangler  is that the same sexist motives of the murderer run rampant in other areas of society, often working against the women aiming to bring forth justice
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Boston Strangler isn’t a true crime film that hits Fincher heights, but it’s still an incredibly fast-paced and gripping story of tense, hard-hitting journalism.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: Not nearly as powerful as other, similar films.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Here, as in real life, the absence of any sort of forward momentum creates a vacuum which is only filled by wild speculation.
reviews.author: Andrew Dignan

reviews.text: While Ruskin decides against showing the horrific acts of violence in brutal detail, the movie still possesses a dark and gritty Fincher-like feel thanks to Ben Kutchins’ moody cinematography and Paul Leonard-Morgan’s simple yet ominous score.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: You don’t have to be a crime reporter to admire McLaughlin and Cole, and the muted tone is fitting.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: The movie's beginning suggests it wants to be a newspaper story, and by the film's end, I got the impression it wanted to be a true-crime series. The uncertainty of tone and theme certainly made for a mixed bag.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Knightley and Coon make a fine team of crime-solving reporters in early 1960s Boston crime drama.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: A distant cousin to Zodiac, with splashes of Seven mixed into its homages, this thriller falls short of its influences yet carves out a small space of its own.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: Ruskin succeeds in paying tribute to Loretta McLaughlin and Jean Cole's hard work, but it's less successful in filling in the larger story.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: ... offers some obligatory twists and turns without digging beneath the surface — like its tenacious wordsmiths would have done.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: If “Boston Strangler” wants us to buy its multiple-killer theory, it would help if we could trust this movie enough to believe what we’re being sold.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: All but one of the Boston Strangler cases are still unresolved, allowing the film to craft a narrative of “what really happened.” And while there’s some speculation and hedging in the movie, its overall explanation seems quite plausible.
reviews.author: Collin Garbarino

reviews.text: The focus is not on the killer or the police, but on the two reporters for the old Boston Record-American who found that reporting the mystery was only one of the many problems that they faced.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: It’s frustrating that this immense, immersive true-crime story has been squeezed into a two-hour movie instead of a series about the two women reporters—superbly played by Keira Knightley and Carrie Coon—who broke a notorious case the police could not.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: But for all of the film’s star power, this look at one of the most infamous murderers ever is too cold and aloof for its own good.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Not even a strong cast led by Keira Knightley and Carrie Coon can save Matt Ruskin’s surface-level true-crime drama.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: This takes the true crime element and reconfigures it as a study of gender dynamics, the balance between the police and media, and the determination of those working to crack the case.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: The film has a few flawed moments of trumped-up drama where there doesn’t need to be any, but beyond that, it feels believable and beautifully driven, much like its protagonists.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Writer/director Matt Ruskin's Boston Strangler is far more fascinating for the conclusion it arrives at than for the process it takes to get there.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The final result is a harrowing and powerful film. Boston Strangler is filled to the brim with tension and a hard hitting investigation ripped from the headlines.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: The Boston Strangler is a standard but solid approach to the true-crime drama, anchored by a great Keira Knightley performance and strong direction.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: Knightley, Chris Cooper and Carrie Coon can’t fix a plodding, unfocused script.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: With cinematographer Ben Kutchins lensing in effectively unsettling, saturated and almost sickly tones of green and brown and gray, and a soundtrack with period-piece tunes, we’re plunged into the world of Boston in the early 1960s.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: The languid pace and lack of finality could turn off those looking for a traditional serial killer romp, but for a thoughtful period piece, with central themes are as relevant in 2023 as they were in 1963, this is good-value weekend viewing.
reviews.author: Chris Newbould

reviews.text: Writer-director Matt Ruskin has done a terrific job of creating a sense of space and place for his true-crime drama.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Knightley, enjoying her most interesting film role since 2018’s Colette, tucks into the project with intelligent vigor. It’s a calm and confident performance that matches Ruskin’s solemn tone.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: It's a reasonably satisfying procedural, but it offers a fairly superficial examination of the deeper issues surrounding the investigation.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: It's a crime drama, ticking away softly as events unfold. Some scenes unnerve, slowly, breathing in order to allow the impact to become clear. ... Keira Knightley gives her finest performance to date.
reviews.author: Peter Martin

reviews.text: This all seems ripe for a great thriller, so why does "Boston Strangler" end up feeling so bland?
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: [Keira] Knightley, [Carrie] Coon, and [Chris] Cooper are a formidable cast, and it’s exciting to see another addition to the small canon of films about female journalists.
reviews.author: Nicole Ackman

reviews.text: Knightley and Coon are a particularly solid dramatic team to give the film the necessary suspense and pathos.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: One of the most shamelessly pandering pictures I’ve seen in some time.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: It has one thing to say, and it says it over and over again with a dismal lack of nuance.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: The material deserves a more comprehensive treatment... which leads Ruskin’s film to feel unsatisfying for those expecting either a thriller, a character study, or an expose on misogyny tinted corruption.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: The movie attempts to serve multiple narrative masters, but ends up coming across as vague and indistinct.
reviews.author: Brent Simon

reviews.text: This highly watchable telling of the infamous 60s-era murder case winningly puts the spotlight on the female reporters who battled systemic sexism to tell the story.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: “Boston Strangler” is a scatterbrained recollection that’s reminiscent of a Wikipedia synopsis and it undervalues the lengths and courage it took from its main subjects to crack the case and, in the process, put their families at risk.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: “Boston Strangler” may muddle its facts, but its message never wavers. In a genre dominated by perfunctory intrigue, how exhilarating to see a film with morals this clear, consistent, and touching.
reviews.author: Lena Wilson

reviews.text: "These women — their deaths, their names, their lives, their pain — are regarded by the camera as little more than a morbid spectacle, which is jarring against the film's supposed message."
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: The telling of this fascinating investigation deals with many of our current issues, like sexism in the workplace, misogyny and cover-up by the police departments involved and the fear of violence and crime.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Boston Strangler is a competent look at how incompetence assisted a serial killer.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Boston Strangler is an engrossing and, at times, spinetingling crime film told with a captivating sleuth-like obsession.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: There is a life-threatening lack of oomph in the picture. Carrie Coon is the only spark, as the seen-it-all tough gal reporter with a "screw you" attitude.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: While it takes its time to find its footing, BOSTON STRANGLER still surprises with the twists and turns drawn from its true crime origins.
reviews.author: Sarah Musnicky

reviews.text: Smart and powerfully understated.
reviews.author: Sheri Linden

reviews.text: You don’t have to look further than the pedestrian title to guess that Matt Ruskin’s “Boston Strangler” is a spiritless affair.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: There is so little dramatic excitement to any of this. Where is the tension? Where is the suspense? Where is the macabre horror?
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: The cast keeps “Boston Strangler” involving, with Ruskin unable to sustain initial stretches of discovery for the entire run time.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: An intriguing murder mystery film that showcases the effort good reporters put in, and the sacrifices they make.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Ruskin’s examination of the social and political elements that enabled the Strangler is bold. In his next film, he should apply that same boldness toward an aesthetic purpose, too.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: The Boston Strangler offers a lot of good. It is a solid drama that centers on two women fighting against great odds to tell the truth.
reviews.author: Ferdosa Abdi

reviews.text: Even though “Boston Strangler” lacks the oomph needed for a gripping serial killer chase, its focus on journalism and the power that women in newsrooms bring is a shining aspect.
reviews.author: Ema Sasic

reviews.text: Clocking in at a lean 112 minutes, Boston Strangler flies through months and years within single sequences, keen to arrive at the next pivotal moment in the investigation — even if it means sacrificing exploring its central figures with more depth.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Whether viewed as a serial killer yarn or an inspirational story about women overcoming gender biases, the film remains close to its antecedents but delivers a solid drama that will appeal to today’s amateur sleuths and true crime enthusiasts.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Boston Strangler is a compelling, if occasionally uneven depiction of the struggles of ambitious professional women in the 60s. Call it Zodiac-lite
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: Boston Strangler is a beige and grey looking procedural, devoid of genuine suspense or drama; stuck between wanting to be a traditional narrative about catching a mass murderer and women being underestimated by a patriarchal, sexist power structure.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Despite dependable performances from Knightley and Coon, who honestly couldn’t be bad in anything, Boston Strangler is workmanlike above all, a drab procedural that showcases the overlapping conflicts of their professional and personal lives.
reviews.author: Christian Gallichio

reviews.text: While watching “Boston Strangler,” I was reminded time and again of David Fincher’s “Zodiac,” a movie I wouldn’t be surprised to learn Ruskin had studied in preparation for this.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Given the popularity of true crime, the murder aspect of Boston Strangler is the hook, but the story is deepened by its portrait of the importance of journalism to uncover the truth, and the intrepid reporters who do the work, despite the consequences.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Even two of the most established actors working today can’t salvage the shoddy script.
reviews.author: Emma Kiely

reviews.text: While the film’s determination to spotlight the women who brought down the Boston Strangler over the killer himself is admirable, it leaves a hole in the middle of the film that nothing else really manages to fill.
reviews.author: Ross McIndoe

reviews.text: Zodiac Lite.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Packed with solid performances from Oscar winners and nominees alike, 'Boston Strangler' delivers on all fronts as Keira Knightley, Carrie Coon, and Chris Cooper bring it home for Hulu.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: On the surface of it, Boston Strangler is a very routine-looking thriller with a topical wrinkle... And yet something happens in the movie’s last quarter, as the crimes’ pattern begins to spread itself out, like a stain on the sheets.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: Solid, but unspectacular, dramatization that shows female journalists on the forefront of an important investigation while facing unique challenges due to sexism. Knightley does excellent work & there's just enough cinematic style to keep it interesting.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: A two-hour film isn’t enough time to tell such a complex story... a miniseries would’ve served the twists and turns best, but nonetheless, this take on the material is a noble examination, if not a thorough one.
reviews.author: Jeff York

synopsis: Loretta McLaughlin becomes the first journalist to connect the Boston Strangler murders. As the mysterious killer claims more and more victims, Loretta attempts to continue her investigation alongside colleague and confidante Jean Cole.
